evidenceAudit.scope: Adult and child identification of familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) in primary care, referral for DNA testing and specialist review, cascade testing, statin target and pregnancy advice, from NICE CG71.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The Simon Broome criteria and Dutch Lipid Clinic Network point values are in CG71 appendices that were not opened.
No Saudi national FH guideline was opened.
Statin dosing frequency, renal and hepatic adjustments and SFDA registration were not verified.
CG71 dates from 2008 with later updates; later lipid guidance (NICE NG238) was not compared here.
Paediatric statin doses are in the British National Formulary for Children and were not opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: FH is characterised by raised low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and premature coronary heart disease (CHD), defined in CG71 as a coronary event before 60 years of age in the patient or a first-degree relative. Diagnosis combines cholesterol level, personal and family history, tendon xanthomata and DNA testing. An identified disease-causing mutation gives an unequivocal diagnosis even if LDL-C does not meet the criteria. Homozygous FH, including compound heterozygous FH, carries similarly high cardiovascular risk. Cascade testing uses DNA testing to find affected first-, second- and, where possible, third-degree relatives.

references.title: NICE CG71: Familial hypercholesterolaemia: identification and management

symptoms: Usually none until coronary events occur.
Family history of premature CHD or very high cholesterol.
Chest pain or other CHD symptoms in a person with a raised cholesterol.
physicalSigns: Tendon xanthomata; their absence does not exclude FH.
redFlags: LDL-C above 13 mmol/L in an adult, or above 11 mmol/L in a child or young person: consider homozygous FH.
Premature CHD symptoms in a person with suspected FH.
Conception while taking a statin: stop at once and refer urgently to obstetrics for fetal assessment.
precipitants: Secondary causes of raised cholesterol, which must be excluded before diagnosing FH.
A first-degree relative with premature CHD or with a confirmed FH mutation.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Exclude secondary causes before an FH diagnosis; the cholesterol falls when the cause is treated.

differentials.condition: Relative who tests negative for the family mutation

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Above 7.5 mmol/L (above 9.0 mmol/L at 30 or over in a record search)
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Triggers FH assessment; offer measurement if premature CHD in the person or a first-degree relative and no level is known.
ruleIn.normalValue: Below the CG71 suspicion threshold of 7.5 mmol/L; local laboratory range applies

clinicalManagement.title: Identify possible FH
actions: Suspect FH in adults with total cholesterol above 7.5 mmol/L or a personal or family history of premature CHD.
Search records for under-30s with total cholesterol above 7.5 mmol/L and people aged 30 or over with total cholesterol above 9.0 mmol/L.
Exclude secondary causes first; do not use QRISK2 or Framingham risk tools in FH.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm and refer
actions: Confirm with two LDL-C measurements and score with Simon Broome or Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria.
Refer for DNA testing if possible or definite FH, or Dutch Lipid Clinic Network score above 5.
Refer all people with FH to an FH specialist for confirmation and to start cascade testing.
CG71 defines urgent referral as as soon as possible with a maximum of 14 days.

clinicalManagement.title: Start and titrate lipid-lowering treatment
actions: Offer a high-intensity statin with the lowest acquisition cost, aiming for at least a 50% LDL-C reduction.
Increase to the maximum licensed or tolerated dose if a reduction above 50% is not reached.
If maximum tolerated high-intensity statin plus ezetimibe does not give above 50%, refer to an FH specialist.
Tell adults that treatment is lifelong.

clinicalManagement.title: Children and young people
actions: Offer a DNA test to children aged 0–10 with one affected parent at the earliest opportunity, and again if not tested by age 10.
Refer to a child- and young person-focused FH service; offer a statin by age 10 or at the earliest opportunity afterwards.

clinicalManagement.title: Pregnancy and contraception
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At first consideration of treatment, then at least annually
actions: Discuss pregnancy risks when lipid-modifying therapy is first considered and revisit at least annually.
Stop lipid-modifying treatment 3 months before trying to conceive; if conception occurs on a statin, stop at once and refer urgently to obstetrics.
Combined oral contraceptives are not generally contraindicated, but consider other methods because of a small possible rise in cardiovascular risk.
Do not routinely measure cholesterol during pregnancy.

medicationPlan.note: CG71 defines high-intensity statins as atorvastatin 20 to 80 mg and rosuvastatin 10 to 40 mg and requires at least a 50% LDL-C reduction. Dosing frequency, renal and hepatic adjustment, interactions and SFDA registration were not verified; follow the product information and hospital formulary. Paediatric doses use the British National Formulary for Children (not opened).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Total cholesterol above 7.5 mmol/L, or personal or family history of premature CHD (Rec 1.1.1).
Total cholesterol above 7.5 mmol/L under age 30, or above 9.0 mmol/L at age 30 or over (Rec 1.1.2).
Simon Broome possible or definite FH, or Dutch Lipid Clinic Network score above 5 (Rec 1.1.6).
LDL-C above 13 mmol/L in adults or above 11 mmol/L in children and young people (Rec 1.1.8).

teaching.scope: Adult and child identification of familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) in primary care, referral for DNA testing and specialist review, cascade testing, statin target and pregnancy advice, from NICE CG71.
learningObjectives: Apply CG71 case-finding thresholds in primary care.
Refer for DNA testing and cascade testing.
pitfalls: Using QRISK2 or Framingham in FH.
Diagnosing FH before secondary causes are excluded.
keyPoints: FH is suspected at total cholesterol above 7.5 mmol/L with or without premature CHD.
The statin goal is at least a 50% LDL-C fall.
A negative mutation test in a relative returns them to general-population care.

references.title: NICE CG71: Familial hypercholesterolaemia: identification and management

patientEducation: Explain that FH is inherited and that treatment is lifelong.
Advise relatives to have cascade testing through the FH service.
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking, healthy diet and regular physical activity; review at each annual structured review.
mdtReferrals: FH specialist service; paediatric FH service for children; obstetrics and cardiology shared care in pregnancy; family-tracing (cascade testing) team.
dischargeCriteria: Not applicable as an admission topic; transfer to shared care once the specialist plan and statin target are set.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Structured review at least annually, covering CHD symptoms, smoking, fasting lipid profile, adherence and side effects, and cascade testing progress.
